name: Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis, Roman Law Codified
summary: Emperor Justinian I commissions the legal scholar Tribonian to compile and codify all Roman law. The resulting Corpus Juris Civilis (529-534) consists of the Code (imperial rescripts), the Digest (jurists' opinions), the Institutes (student textbook), and the Novels (new laws). It systematizes 1,000 years of Roman legal development into a coherent framework.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Corpus Juris Civilis is one of the most influential documents in Western history; rediscovered in Italy (11th century) and taught at Bologna from the 12th century, it becomes the foundation of continental European civil law tradition (France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Louisiana); the distinction between Justinian civil law and English common law tradition is a fundamental division in modern legal systems
